title.narrative: Second Greater Mekong Subregion Tourism Infrastructure for Inclusive Growth Project

description.narrative: The project will help transform secondary towns in the Greater Mekong Subregion (GMS) eastern economic corridor into economically inclusive, competitive tourism destinations by improving transport infrastructure, urban sanitation, and capacity to sustainably manage tourism growth. It will boost trade in services by promoting cross-border tourism and deepen GMS and Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) regional cooperation and integration. About 168,000 residents are expected to benefit from climate-resilient infrastructure development, improved urban greenspace, cleaner beaches, and better access to economic opportunities.

Status of Implementation Progress: Overachieved.
The ASEAN Tourism Standards Certification Board operates at the national level, certifying entities that meet ASEAN tourism standards. The Board comprises of 7 members, 4 males and 3 females. At the provincial level, the Department of Tourism acts as an advisory unit, receiving applications, conducting initial assessments, and submitting them to the national certification board for final evaluation and certification.
Partly achieved.
Thua Thien Hue has received the certification of green hotel for 3 hotels/resorts (Pilgrimage Village in 2018, Vedana Lagoon Resort & Spa in 2022, and Azerai La Residence in 2024).
For Hoa Binh, Nghe An, Quang Binh, and Quang Tri, The Departments of Tourism have implemented the dissemination and propaganda of ASEAN tourism standards as well as its benefits to all organizations/units operating in the field of tourism in the provinces.
The target of 44 hotels being certified ASEAN Green Hotel Standard is not feasible for the following reasons:
1. ASEAN Tourism Awards:
- There are various types of awards, each with specific quotas.
- Each country also has a quota (maximum of 5 awards per year), and some awards are not available annually.
2. Varying interest among tourism businesses/accommodation facilities:
- The interest level of tourism businesses and accommodation facilities varies independently of state management agencies. Although MCST conducted extensive outreach, training, and promotional activities to raise service quality and awareness, participation remained limited.
3. Unfeasible design:
- Four- and five-star hotels already adhere to existing standards, so obtaining ASEAN certification does not offer clear benefits to these entities.
4. Impact of COVID-19 during 20202022: no immediate need for certification.
Partly achieved. Only Hue City received the certification as a clean tourist city in 2018 and in 2024.
The target could not be achieved due to the limited local capacity and resources in the provinces of Hoa Binh, Nghe An, Quang Binh, and Quang Tri to meet the extensive certification criteria, which required more time and investment than initially anticipated. These provinces have implemented sanitation programs, including the installation of mobile smart toilets and environmentally friendly trash cans, to improve their infrastructure.
Overachieved.

Except for Quang Binh, all other subprojects have prepared or are in the process of preparing O&M plans for the infrastructure built using project funds. Quang Binh will develop O&M plan in 2025 and put into implementation after the physical work completed.
Financial planning for maintenance follows the current legal regulations.
PPP proposals for 4 subprojects have been prepared.
-Hoa Binh: Tien pagoda parking yard O&M service including collection of public service fees.
-Quang Binh: Nhat Le river cruise pier O&M partnership.
-Quang Tri: Cua Viet beach O&M service including collection of public service fees.
-Hue: Hue river piers O&M partnerships: one for 5 piers on Huong river, one for Da Bac pier, and one for Con Toc-Vinh Tu piers.
For Hue, a PPP international consultant (funded by TA 6899-REG: Southeast Asia Sustainable Tourism Facility) is helping to develop a financial model for the proposed PPP approach O&M contract.
A total of 39 consultation meetings were conducted of which 472 out of 1,010 participants were female.
The construction of the 4.3 km embankment and sidewalk along Cua Lo Beach in Nghe An was completed. The work has contributed to flood protection and drainage improvements for an area of 286 hectares.
Data will be collected after the facilities are in full operation.
A total of 28 km of access roads to tourist sites has been completed across five provinces.
- In Hue, the construction of 8.6 km of access roads was completed.
- In Hoa Binh, 11 km of access roads was completed.
- In Nghe An, the construction of a 3.7 km access road to Ru Gam Pagoda was completed.
- In Quang Tri, the construction of a 368 m road linking Highway 9D to the tourist port was completed.
- In Quang Binh, the construction of 4 km of roads has achieved 95% physical completion. 5% of connection to the national highway is being finalized.
In total, 7 out of 13 passenger piers across five subprojects have been completed.
- In Hue, 6 of 8 piers are finished, with Bao Vinh Pier delayed by LAR issues and expected to be completed by June 2025 using counterpart funds and 5 Le Loi Pier transferred to a private investor's project.
- In Quang Tri, 1 pier has been completed.
- In Quang Binh, 4 piers are under construction with 70% physical progress.
